title: The PWA status bar is opaque and theme-color owns its colour
context: From iOS 26 a standalone web app that draws under the status bar (black-translucent with viewport-fit=cover) gets the Liquid Glass scroll edge effect: a blur band reaching about 40pt below the status bar that washed out the header on iOS 27. No CSS or meta switch disables it. On a real iOS 27 device, switching to the default status bar style removed the blur while the page was at rest.
decision: The standalone PWA uses the default, opaque status bar style and no longer draws content under the status bar. The status bar colour comes from the theme-color meta, which each route layout sets through StatusBarColor from its own surface token and which follows the user's resolved light or dark theme.

alternatives.option: Keep black-translucent and cover the blur with a backdrop-filter overlay.
alternatives.reason: WebKit no longer renders a fixed overlay under the status bar in standalone mode.

alternatives.option: Declare theme-color per route through Next.js viewport exports.
alternatives.reason: The server cannot see a user-chosen theme, and every colour would need a second hex copy of the CSS tokens.

consequences: iOS reads the status bar style when the app is added to the Home Screen, so existing installs keep black-translucent until removed and re-added; reverting this decision needs the same reinstall.
env(safe-area-inset-top) is zero in portrait, so every header that pads by it collapses to its own height without further change.
StatusBarColor keeps setting the html and body background as BodyBackdrop did, so an install still on black-translucent sees the same colours as before.
revisitTriggers: iOS offers a way to turn off the scroll edge effect for web apps.
iOS stops applying theme-color changes made after launch.
